newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile leader Frei signs bill to end censorship.
newsitem.headline: Chile leader Frei signs bill to end censorship.

text.p: Chilean President Eduardo Frei sent a bill to Congress on Monday to end film censorship and guarantee artistic freedom by eliminating controls in the country's military-dictated constitution.
Chile's 1980 constitution, written by Gen. Augusto Pinochet's regime, pledges freedom of information for the press, radio and television but maintains film censorship.

"The press, radio, television and whatever other form of publishing words, text and images are protected by the freedom of opinion and information, but this is not so for production and distribution of films," said Frei at the signing ceremony.
"Now the moment has arrived to do away with this contradiction...and put an end to this odious discrimination which only affects the cinema."
The bill proposes eliminating a state board that censors films before they are released to cinemas, replacing it with a system of film classification.

Censorship has grabbed the headlines in the last week with a row between the government and television channels over a state AIDS campaign and new attempts to screen Martin Scorcese's "Last Temptation of Christ" which has been banned by court order.
Before the ceremony, Frei lashed out at the three television stations, two of which are controlled by the Catholic Church, who have refused to show the government's AIDS prevention advertisements.
"The behaviour of these channels is surprising," he told reporters.

"While they censor a campaign which is essential for the health of the population, especially of young people, they regularly include in their programmes scenes that are clearly against the values they say they promote."
A Chilean court upheld in February a 1989 ban on screening "The Last Temptation of Christ", which was considered blasphemous.
